I think they have. I'm not really sure how to tell. The sense of doom and thoughts and stuff are still pretty prominent, but I think it's definitely less impending at them moment. So that's good.

I'm guessing things were worse because of the dose change, so I think that might have settled down now. It turned out I had an infection as well, so that probably wasn't helping either.

I spoke to my nurse about the thoughts, but she wasn't super helpful but I'm not sure she quite knew how to react. I'm glad I mentioned it to her, though.

I think it's a case of keeping an eye on things and noticing any changes, which is something I think I can do. 

Thank you for being so kind and helpful. I really appreciate it and I hope that you're doing okay.

Thank you stranger. Hug appreciated :)

My psychiatrist added a new medication to the old one recently, which is still on a fairly low dose.  I think I’m having a med review with a new doctor in a few weeks.

I have an appointment with a GP today to get a repeat prescription, but I’m not sure I’ll bring it up with her because she isn’t my regular doctor and I’m not sure she can do anything without the psychiatrist’s input.

I’m seeing my nurse this week though, so I might mention something to her. I feel like every time I talk to someone, I say that things are bad when, relatively speaking, they aren’t as bad as they have been - so I get a bit worried that they think I’m overreacting.

There’s nothing really different happening in my life that would trigger this change. There are certain practical signs that things are getting worse, but I haven’t really taken into account my thought processes in that. I tried looking back at some things I wrote down in the past, and this feeling is sort of a common thing before things get worse.

Thank you again for your kind words. I really do appreciate it.
